summary: A worker-placement game about gathering resources, building landmarks, and advancing the cathedral, with a virtue/corruption track that lets you steal workers or dodge the black market at moral cost. It plays as a tight engine-builder with light take-that (sending rivals' workers to jail) layered on top of otherwise fairly parallel development.
praised: Clean, tightly interlocking worker-placement systems (money, resources, apprentices, virtue) that all feed into each other
The virtue/corruption mechanic adds thematic tension and meaningful decisions
Strong solo mode and good scaling across player counts
High production values and evocative medieval theme
The 'kill steal'/jailing mechanic gives worker placement rare teeth without full conflict
criticised: Can feel a bit dry or math-y/optimization-heavy for players wanting more narrative or interaction
Jailing/sending workers to the block can feel mean or swingy at 2 players
Some rules overhead and iconography to learn early on
Randomness in contract/building card draws can limit planning
Runs long for its weight class at higher player counts

interaction.kind: worker denial and occasional direct sabotage (jailing/robbing rivals) layered over parallel engine-building

scoring.why: Points come from buildings constructed, cathedral contributions, virtue/end-game bonuses, and leftover resources/money, so efficient multi-track engine building decides the winner
